regulatory_note: Hawaii environmental review and the Superferry precedent gate inter-island service; US Coast Guard Subchapter T applies; Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors controls Honokōhau, Kawaihae and Hilo berths.
seasonality: The leeward Kona/Kohala coast is calm year-round; winter swell and whale season (Dec–Apr) affect channel crossings and impose speed discipline.
summary: Hawaiʻi Island's leeward Kona/Kohala coast carries the island's luxury resort mass — the Kohala Coast hosts Four Seasons Hualālai, Mauna Lani (Auberge), Mauna Kea Beach Hotel and Fairmont Orchid — while Kailua-Kona and Honokōhau are the visitor and small-boat hubs and Hilo anchors the windward working side. Calm leeward water, sheltered by Mauna Kea and Hualālai, makes the Kona–Kohala corridor an excellent all-electric resort-transfer run. Kawaihae is the deep-draft harbor and the Hawaiʻi-side terminus of the ʻAlenuihāhā crossing to Maui — among the roughest channels on Earth, and therefore Navier's headline seasickness-relief corridor.
tagline: The Big Island's calm leeward resort coast and the Hawaiʻi-side endpoint of the ʻAlenuihāhā seasickness-relief crossing.
